newsitem.title: CANADA: Viceroy Homes shrs plunge after earnings.
newsitem.headline: Viceroy Homes shrs plunge after earnings.

text.p: Viceroy Homes Ltd shares lost almost half their value on Friday after the company reported lower-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings.
Viceroy shares fell C$5.05 to C$5.35 in early afternoon trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange on volume of more than 350,000 shares.
Shares of the Toronto-based maker of pre-engineered housing fell after the company said that both sales and net earnings fell in the third quarter from a year earlier.
Viceroy's sales fell 22 percent to C$11 million in the third quarter from a year earlier. Net income for the quarter fell 61 percent to C$409,000.
"The problem with Viceroy of course was earnings," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading with ScotiaMcLeod Inc. "I think that they're getting strong competition."

In a press release the company attributed the decline to "an expected drop in domestic sales" and "a new, potentially large Japanese customer's orders not materializing because of the customer's internal delays."

The company also noted that since September the Japanese yen has seen a sharp drop in value against the Canadian dollar, making Viceroy's product more expensive in Japan. Japan is a major market for Viceroy.
Ketchen noted that the company faces strong competition from other makers of pre-engineered housing including Royal Plastics Group Ltd.
Viceroy Homes officials could not immediately be reached for comment on the share price drop.
Viceroy also announced in the earnings statement that it was proceeding with plans to establish western production facilities.
